briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Repeal Momentum Builds in Lansing While DEA and Psychedelics Push Forward Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan operators are getting real ammunition against the 24% wholesale tax as revenue keeps missing projections and a bipartisan repeal bill lands in Lansing, even as new hospitality-forward stores and settled enforcement fights show the market still has room to innovate. Nationally, the DEA's rescheduling hearing record is tilting toward Schedule III, Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy just got a fast-track FDA voucher, and MSOs are chasing growth through aggressive M&A.

local.text: Jars Cannabis, a retail chain with reportedly 54 stores across Michigan, Arizona, and Colorado, reached an agreement with Madison Heights city authorities to remove a Flock surveillance camera that had been aimed at the store's parking lot entrance, which had been required under a settlement resolving a 2022 licensing lawsuit. A clean win for operators still fighting municipal overreach post-licensing.

Fields Cannary represents a fully integrated cannabis hospitality model combining retail, on-site consumption, dining, and event licensing under one roof, testing whether a winery-style elevated experience can support higher price points in Muskegon. The $4M build targets a fall opening — a blueprint for operators looking to escape commodity-flower price wars.

A bipartisan coalition filed legislation to eliminate the newly implemented wholesale tax, with the sponsor calling it 'unnecessary.' It's the clearest legislative path yet for operators pushing to unwind the 24% levy before it does more damage.

Republican gubernatorial nominee John James is promising to repeal or significantly roll back the 24% wholesale cannabis tax if elected in November, arguing the levy 'drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections.' Whichever way the race breaks, tax relief is now a live campaign issue operators can lean on.

The 24% wholesale tax generated just $37.38 million in Q2 2026, up slightly from $34 million in Q1 but a fraction of the projected $105 million per quarter, leaving the state's $73.4 million total collected so far well short of its $315 million fiscal-year estimate. The shortfall is the strongest evidence yet that Lansing overreached — and the best case for the repeal push gaining steam.

national.text: In closing arguments over cannabis rescheduling, even Bertha Madras, a Harvard psychiatry professor called by anti-rescheduling group SAM, is cited approvingly by the DEA for testimony supporting accepted use for neuropathic pain and cancer-related appetite loss. A shift to Schedule III would preserve federal prohibition while easing tax burdens on state-licensed operators, eliminating 280E penalties and cutting effective tax rates from 60% to the mid-20s.

The FDA has granted Compass Pathways a rolling review for its psilocybin therapy COMP360 in treatment-resistant depression, while also awarding the NDA a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher that could shorten the review to one to two months after filing. The agency has also scheduled a public hearing on the future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs for September 14, 2026.

Curaleaf intends to launch a takeover bid for all outstanding Aurora Cannabis shares, offering $4 per share in a mix of stock and cash, creating a combined company operating in 17 countries with more than $1.5 billion in trailing revenue and nearly $350 million in adjusted earnings. Aurora's board has pushed back, but the bid signals real consolidation appetite among MSOs.

A newly closed deal makes Cresco Pennsylvania's No. 1 MMJ retailer and wholesaler, deepening its grip on the second-largest U.S. medical market. More proof that scaled operators keep finding room to expand even as smaller markets consolidate.

President Trump signed H.R. 6500, temporarily delaying most new federal hemp restrictions from November 12 until December 11, though restrictions on cannabinoids that cannot occur naturally in cannabis will still take effect November 12. A short reprieve, but it buys hemp-adjacent brands critical time to reformulate before the hard deadline hits.
